gloss.w.mouwen.lit: the hands out of the sleeves
gloss.w.handje.lit: to help with a little hand
gloss.w.knie: to know how to do it well
gloss.w.knie.lit: to have it under the knee
gloss.s.easy.1: That little job is very easy.
gloss.s.easy.2: The work is going very well.
gloss.s.easy.3: Come on, let us get to work.
gloss.c.easy.q: Can you help for a moment?
gloss.c.easy.a.why: "Een handje helpen" is asking for help: a yes and coming over.
gloss.w.aandebel: to warn others that something is wrong
gloss.w.deur: to say it straight away, without a long start
gloss.w.deur.lit: to fall into the house with the door
gloss.w.blad: to say honestly what you think
gloss.w.blad.lit: to put no leaf in front of your mouth
gloss.s.plain.1: Speak up when it is not safe.
gloss.s.plain.3: I will get straight to the point.
gloss.c.plain.a: Then I will take the bus today.
gloss.c.plain.a.why: Very hard rain: the bus keeps you dry.
gloss.c.easy: Sayings: the words mean something else
gloss.c.easy.b: Dutch people often use sayings, also at work. The words say one thing, but they mean something else. "Een eitje" is a little egg, but it means: very easy. You do not need to use sayings yourself. You do not understand a saying? Then just ask what it means.
gloss.c.easy.p: What do you mean by that?
gloss.c.easy.s: Your colleague looks at the new task and says: "Dat is een eitje!" What does he mean?
gloss.c.easy.o2: He wants to eat an egg.
gloss.c.easy.w: "Een eitje" means: very easy. Your colleague thinks the task will go quickly.
gloss.c.plain.b: Dutch colleagues often say directly what they think. Sometimes they start with a saying: "Ik neem geen blad voor de mond." That means: I will say honestly what I think. It is not meant to be rude. You may also say honestly what you think, in a calm way.
gloss.c.plain.p: May I say honestly what I think?
gloss.c.plain.s: Your supervisor says: "Ik neem geen blad voor de mond." What does she mean?
gloss.c.plain.o1: She will say honestly what she thinks.
gloss.c.plain.o2: She does not want to talk.
gloss.c.plain.w: "Geen blad voor de mond nemen" means: saying honestly and directly what you think. Many Dutch people find that normal at work.
gloss.zg.zeil.lit: Will you keep a little eye on the sail?
gloss.zg.zeil.m: Will you watch that everything goes well and safely?
gloss.zg.zeil.s: Your supervisor has to leave for a moment. She says: "Hou je een oogje in het zeil?" What does she mean?
gloss.zg.zeil.o1: Watch that everything goes well while she is away.
gloss.zg.zeil.o2: Go and look at a boat.
gloss.zg.zeil.o3: Close your eyes for a moment.
gloss.zg.zeil.w: "Een oogje in het zeil houden" means: paying attention that everything goes well. Not sure what to watch? Ask her before she goes.
gloss.zg.lekker.s: A colleague calls you in the morning: "Ik voel me niet lekker." What does he mean?
gloss.zg.lekker.o2: He did not like his breakfast.
gloss.zg.lekker.w: "Lekker" is also about food, but "niet lekker" here means: a bit ill. You can say it yourself when you call in sick.
gloss.zg.batterij.lit: I am going to charge my battery.
gloss.zg.batterij.m: I am going to rest, so I have energy again.
gloss.zg.batterij.s: Before her days off your colleague says: "Ik ga even mijn batterij opladen." What does she mean?
gloss.zg.batterij.o3: She is going to work extra hours.
gloss.zg.batterij.w: In this saying people are like phones: after rest you have energy again. Days off are for that.
gloss.zg.pluis.m: Something is wrong, or not to be trusted.
gloss.zg.pluis.s: You tell a friend about a job: no contract, pay in cash, and you must give your passport. Your friend says: "Er is iets niet pluis." What does he mean?
gloss.zg.pluis.o1: Something about this job is wrong.
gloss.zg.pluis.o2: The job is soft and nice.
gloss.zg.pluis.w: "Niet pluis" means: not right, not to be trusted. No contract and giving away your passport are warning signs.
gloss.zg.oefening.m: If you practise a lot, you get good at it.
gloss.zg.oefening.s: You find the course hard. Your teacher says: "Oefening baart kunst." What does she mean?
gloss.zg.oefening.o1: Keep practising, then you will get good at it.
gloss.zg.oefening.o2: You must go to an art lesson.
gloss.zg.oefening.o3: Stop, it is too hard for you.
gloss.zg.oefening.w: This is a proverb: with practice you get better. It is true for learning Dutch too.
gloss.zg.zwartwit.lit: Ask for it black on white.
gloss.zg.zwartwit.m: Ask for it on paper, in writing.
gloss.zg.zwartwit.s: Your boss promises you more pay. Your colleague says: "Vraag het zwart op wit." What does she mean?
gloss.zg.zwartwit.o1: Ask for the promise in writing.
gloss.zg.zwartwit.o2: Ask for black and white paper.
gloss.zg.zwartwit.w: Something in writing is proof. For pay, hours and your contract, ask for it "zwart op wit".
gloss.zg.temooi.lit: That is too beautiful to be true.
gloss.zg.temooi.m: It sounds so good that it is probably not true.
gloss.zg.temooi.s: You get a message: "You won 1,000 euros! Send your bank details." Your neighbour says: "Dat is te mooi om waar te zijn." What does she mean?
gloss.zg.temooi.o2: You are lucky: send them quickly.
gloss.zg.temooi.w: Offers that sound too good are often scams. Never send your bank details.
gloss.zg.haast.m: When you rush, things often go wrong.
gloss.zg.haast.s: You are late and you want to cycle through a red light. Your colleague says: "Haastige spoed is zelden goed." What does he mean?
gloss.zg.haast.o1: Do not rush: it is not safe.
gloss.zg.haast.w: This proverb means: rushing often goes wrong. Better a few minutes late than an accident.
gloss.zg.waagt.lit: Who does not dare, does not win.
gloss.zg.waagt.m: You have to try, or you can never succeed.
gloss.zg.waagt.s: You see a job, but you think your Dutch is not good enough. Your coach says: "Wie niet waagt, die niet wint." What does she mean?
gloss.zg.waagt.o1: Just apply: you can only get it if you try.
gloss.zg.waagt.o2: Do not apply for this job.
gloss.zg.waagt.o3: You must play a game to win.
gloss.zg.waagt.w: This proverb tells you to try. Applying costs little, and you learn something from every try.
gloss.zg.koning.m: The customer is very important: help them well and in a friendly way.
gloss.zg.koning.s: A customer is a bit unfriendly. Your supervisor says: "De klant is koning." What does he mean?
gloss.zg.koning.o1: Stay friendly and help the customer well.
gloss.zg.koning.o2: The customer is a real king.
gloss.zg.koning.w: In a shop the customer comes first, so you stay polite. Is a customer rude or threatening? Then get your supervisor.
gloss.zg.tijdgeld.m: Time is valuable: do not waste it.
gloss.zg.tijdgeld.s: Your boss wants the truck loaded quickly. He says: "Tijd is geld." What does he mean?
gloss.zg.tijdgeld.o1: Working time costs money, so work without wasting time.
gloss.zg.tijdgeld.o2: You get money for coming late.
gloss.zg.tijdgeld.w: This saying means that time is valuable. It is never a reason for unsafe work or hours without pay.
gloss.zg.eindjes.lit: It is hard to tie the little ends together.
gloss.zg.eindjes.m: It is hard to pay for everything with the money you have.
gloss.zg.eindjes.s: A colleague says: "Het is moeilijk om de eindjes aan elkaar te knopen." What does she mean?
gloss.zg.eindjes.o1: She has too little money for everything.
gloss.zg.eindjes.w: Many people know this. Money problems? Ask for help early, for example at your municipality (gemeente).
